name: I've tried this kind of thing before
body: "I've worked with coaches before. I've bought programs like this. None of them worked. I don't think this will be any different."
reframe:
**Primary reframe — The Right Teacher:**

"Yeah, that makes sense. Have you tried things in the past? Did you give them a good crack? Cool. So if you've tried, did it the right way, and it didn't work — maybe there's something going on, like me. I'm dyslexic. I was in the lowest classes — until a teacher came who knew how to teach me. Then I went to the top class.

It wasn't that I was dumb. I just hadn't been taught the way I needed to be taught. The teaching style was right for almost everyone — just not me.

Would you be open to considering you might be one of the 2-3% who need a different approach — and just haven't found the right teacher yet?"
storyResponse:
**Companion analogies:** 📚 The Right Teacher → 💔 Bad First Boyfriend

The Right Teacher reframes failure as fit-mismatch (gentle). Bad First Boyfriend reframes fear as universal (recovery is normal).

name: How exactly does this work?
body: "Before I commit, I need to understand exactly how this works. Walk me through every step. What does Day 1 look like? Day 30? Day 90?"
reframe:
**Reframe — The Plane Ticket:**

"It's completely normal. It's not your job to know exactly how you're gonna get there. When you buy a plane ticket, you don't go to the pilot and ask to inspect the cockpit. That's the pilot's responsibility. Yours is to show up on your flight, strap in, and let's go.

As long as you can show up, we'll do the rest. Are you willing to do that?"
storyResponse:
**Companion analogy:** ✈️ The Plane Ticket

**Companion story:** 🛫 The Pilot and the Plane Ticket (Story Bank).

name: This is just how I am / how it is
body: "I've always been this way. This is just how I operate / how my industry works / how my situation is."
reframe:
**Reframe — Perfect Strategy for Where You Are:**

"Right now you've got the perfect strategy to be exactly where you're meant to be. Whatever you're doing — it's perfectly fine, based on your decisions, thoughts, feelings, actions, and the meaning you've attached to everything in your life.

You've been running an unconscious strategy that has led you up to this point. If you'd like to change, it requires a new YOU — new thinking, new actions, new skills. Otherwise, you'll never change. Right?

So if you continue to make decisions based on who you are right now, you'll never change. That's totally fine by me. I just don't think that's what's best for you. Do you?"
storyResponse:
**Companion analogy:** 🕰️ Perfect Strategy for Where You Are

HEAVY reframe. Earn the right — don't deploy in the first 15 minutes. Best paired with the prospect having already shared a specific stuck-pattern that you can mirror back as 'see, here's the pattern.'

name: I want to talk to my partner / spouse first
body: "This sounds great but I want to run it by my husband / wife / partner first before I commit."
reframe:
**Discovery questions BEFORE reframing:**
1. "Totally understand. What specifically would you want their input on?"
2. "Have you and [partner] talked about [the problem] before? What does [partner] think?"
3. "Are they typically supportive of investment decisions?"

**If genuine consultation needed:** Set up a 3-way call — don't push past it.

**If used as delay (most common):** Use 🛣️ Fork in the Road. "Right now you're at a fork in the road. Stay where you are, OR talk to [partner] tonight and get on the same page about getting where you both want to go. Which is it?"
storyResponse:
**Companion analogies:** 🛣️ Fork in the Road → 🏁 The Finish Line

**Critical:** ALWAYS treat as legit on first mention. Steamrolling a real partner consult loses the deal AND the trust.

name: This is a stretch / I can't really afford it
body: "Look, I want to do this, but it's a real stretch for me right now financially. I'd have to push to make it work."
reframe:
**Reframe — Desert Island Syndrome:**

"I hear you and I appreciate things may be a stretch — we get this a lot. We call it Desert Island Syndrome. Imagine you're trapped on a desert island and you've built a raft. What's the hardest part? Breaking past the surf, right?

That's where you are. The waves are pushing you back. But you're so close — one solid push and you're free. If you don't, the surf keeps pushing you back, and your resources and desire dwindle. Make sense?

I can help you make this stretch. Are you in?"
storyResponse:
**Companion analogy:** 🏝️ Desert Island Syndrome

**Companion story:** 📞 Do-or-Die Phone Call to Dad — deploy if hesitation is partly self-belief.

name: I want to do it on my own
body: "I think I'll just give this a try on my own. I'm a do-it-yourself kind of person."
reframe:
**Reframe — The Plane Ticket (DIY angle):**

"I get it. Can I ask you a question — and let me know if I'm wrong here — but it seems like you're a pretty do-it-yourself type. Am I right? Okay. Suppose you found a proven system that gave you what you wanted. Would it be a challenge to follow that without trying to reinvent the wheel? Or not even an issue?"

**[If they say 'not an issue']** → Plane Ticket close.

**[If they say 'yes, that'd be a challenge']** → Now you know the real objection.
storyResponse:
**Companion analogy:** ✈️ The Plane Ticket

**Backup analogy:** 📚 The Right Teacher

DIY mindset is often a control issue. Plane Ticket dissolves the need for control. Right Teacher reframes solo-effort as fit-mismatch.

name: I don't know if I can do this
body: "What if I fail? What if I'm not good enough for this? I'm scared."
reframe:
**Reframe — Self-Belief / Story-Led:**

Lead with the 📞 Do-or-Die Phone Call to Dad story (Story Bank). Personal testimonial first, then framework:

"It boils down to two things: one, we make decisions from a place of 'what if I fail and we stay stuck?' Or two, we make decisions from 'what if we succeed?' — and we try.

Some decisions don't matter much. Others directly contribute to your success. So — what action do you feel you need to take so when you go to bed tonight, you've done everything you can to make XYZ a reality?"
storyResponse:
**Primary tool:** 📞 Do-or-Die Phone Call to Dad (Story Bank) — use FIRST.

**Companion analogies:** ✈️ The Plane Ticket (relieves the 'how' anxiety) → 🕰️ Perfect Strategy (relieves the 'who am I' anxiety)

Fear-of-failure is identity, not logic. Story before logic.

name: I already know what I need to do
body: "I appreciate the call, but honestly I've thought about this a lot. I know what I need to do — I just need to execute on my plan."
reframe:
**Reframe — Cave Vision:**

"I hear you — you've thought about this and you've got a handle on it. We get this one a lot. We call it Cave Vision.

Imagine you've spent your whole life in a cave, facing a wall of shadows. You've gotten really good at reading those shadows. But you don't know there's a fire behind you, and behind it, a whole world. So when someone says 'come outside,' you fight them — because in your world, the wall IS the world.

It's not that you're wrong — you've read those shadows better than anyone. It's just that they're a small slice of what's going on. Would you be open to having a look at what's outside before you decide?"
storyResponse:
**Companion analogy:** 🕳️ Cave Vision

**Backup analogy:** 📚 The Right Teacher — if their certainty comes from past experience.

name: I don't have time to build this
body: I don't have time to build this
reframe: The full install is three 90-minute sessions. We give you the templates, the field structure, and the click recipe. You're not building from scratch — you're bolting on a prebuilt loop. Most clients are publishing inside a week.
storyResponse: Onboarding timeline screenshot — 'first webinar live in 7 days'

name: My audience is too small
reframe: The loop works on 30 registrants the same way it works on 3,000 — better margins per attendee, in fact. Marisol's $48k case was off a 47-person webinar. Volume is a vanity metric. Conversion + recovery is the real game.
storyResponse: Marisol case study — $48k off a 47-person webinar

name: Let me think about it
body: "This all sounds really good. I just… need to go away and think about it."
reframe:
**Reframe — Penthouse / Ground Floor:**

"That makes sense based on where you're at, right? But the only problem is — if you're always making decisions based off where you are, where you are is the only place you can ever be. Does that make sense?

If you're at the penthouse, you can see far. Ground floor — you can't see anywhere near as much. To make the move, you need the higher perspective. But to get to the penthouse, you have to make the decisions of the person who got there.

So — what are the things you feel you need to do to put yourself in the right position to make that shift?"

**Backup reframe — Fork in the Road:** Use if Penthouse doesn't move them.

**Last-resort — Finish Line:** End-of-call only.
storyResponse:
**Companion analogies:** 🏢 Penthouse / Ground Floor → 🛣️ Fork in the Road → 🏁 The Finish Line

Use this stack in order. Don't escalate to Finish Line unless you've used the first two.

name: I've tried webinars before and they didn't work
body: I've tried webinars before and they didn't work
reframe: You didn't have a webinar problem, you had a pipeline-memory problem. WebinarOS grades your build across 11 dimensions before you ever go live so we find the leaks before your audience does.
storyResponse: Case study — before/after the Readiness Review
proof: Readiness Review screenshot with verdict 🟩 Presentation-Ready

name: I've tried funnels before and they didn't work
body: I've tried funnels before and they didn't work
reframe: This isn't a funnel — it's a loop. Funnels assume linear behavior (click → buy). The loop assumes humans are messy: they ghost, come back, and decide on day 9 instead of day 1. We built for human behavior, not template behavior.
storyResponse: Side-by-side funnel decay vs. loop recovery chart

name: I'm not techy enough
reframe: If you can drag-and-drop a Trello card, you can run HelixOS. The base is pre-built, the automations are pre-wired, and onboarding includes 1:1 setup. We meet you at your skill level — not the other way around.
storyResponse: Loom of a 60-year-old client running their first replay sequence solo

name: It's not the right time
body: "I want to do this. It's just… not the right time. Maybe in a few months / next quarter / after [event]."
reframe:
**Reframe — The Bitcoin Time Machine:**

"Let me ask you something. If I gave you a time machine and sent you back to 2010, where you could find your past self — what would you tell them? Bitcoin in 2010 was 8 cents. Today it's tens of thousands.

Your past self would say 'sounds risky, I'll think about it next year when I've got more.' And you'd want to shake them, right? Because you can see what they can't.

The past version of you wasn't being stupid — they were just making the decision with the information they had. So — if a future version of you, ten years from now, came back to this conversation… what do you reckon they'd be telling you to do?"
storyResponse:
**Companion analogy:** ⏳ The Bitcoin Time Machine

**Companion story:** 🤖 The Bitcoin Time Traveller (Story Bank)

Pair with 🏃 Usain Bolt: Bolt installs vision (gold medal), Bitcoin installs hindsight (future regret). Together they cover both incentives in one beat.

name: I just need more time
body: "It's just… a lot. I need more time before I make a call this big."
reframe:
**Reframe — The Finish Line (last-resort):**

"That's okay if you want more time. But I don't think that's what's best for you given what you told me. We're at the finish line — this is where so many people stop. But you're going to have to do this eventually — now, tomorrow, a year, or ten years. Each delay, the problem gets worse. Committing is the hardest part. After that, you just follow our lead.

Are you in?"
storyResponse:
**Companion analogies:** 🏁 The Finish Line → 🕰️ Perfect Strategy for Where You Are

Finish Line is the close. Perfect Strategy is the deeper mindset shift if Finish Line lands but they don't move — it makes them confront that 'more time' is just running the same pattern.

name: Will this work in my niche?
body: Will this work in my niche?
reframe: We've installed loops for 14+ niches: fitness coaches, real estate brokers, fractional CFOs, pet trainers, even a beekeeper. The mechanic is universal — only the messaging changes. Onboarding includes niche-specific copy review with Danno.
storyResponse: Niche logo wall — 14 industries running the loop

name: This sounds complicated to set up
body: This sounds complicated to set up
reframe: Synchronized Journey is a model, not a tech project. The core install is one Lead State table + three triggers, and you already own every tool you need. Implementation is measured in days, not months.
storyResponse: Origin story — 'the week I stopped rebuilding Zaps'
proof: Screenshot: install checklist finished in 3 sessions

name: I'm doing okay — I just want to grow
body: "Things are alright. I'm doing okay. I just want to grow / get better. There's no urgency."
reframe:
**Reframe — Comfort = Mediocrity:**

"I get it. But comfort is the breeding ground for mediocrity. So you can stay in that breeding ground for another 12, 18 months — or we can start to make the moves to become the person you want to be.

It's up to you. At the end of the day, it's your choice. So what do YOU need to get the outcomes you want for you, your business, and your family?"
storyResponse:
**Companion analogy:** 🌱 Comfort = Mediocrity

**Setup story:** 🏃 Usain Bolt at the YMCA — deploy BEFORE Comfort = Mediocrity to install the gold-medal vision first.
